library.name: Selcon
library.notes: HUFA/B12 enrichment emulsion for the hatchery's enrichment soak — shake well; use less if the water does not clear.

library.name: Reef Juice (live phyto blend)
library.notes: Tank dose only — Reefphyto: 'not designed as a culture feed'. 1 ml per 27 / 18 / 9 L a day for light / medium / heavy stocking (their blog: 2–3× a week is right for most reefs). Into flow at dusk, skimmer + UV off 30–60 min. Gentle shake, never freeze.
library.doseNote: Into the flow at dusk, skimmer and UV off for an hour.

library.name: Rotifer Feed Concentrate
library.notes: The rotifer cone's food: Nannochloropsis oculata + Tetraselmis suecica only. Dose to a leafy green, little and often; top up when the water clears. Not a copepod feed.

library.name: Copepod Feed
library.notes: The Tigriopus tub's food — feed to a Granny Smith apple-skin green, half rate in week one, again when it clears.

library.name: Rotifer & Artemia Enrichment
library.notes: Live Nannochloropsis (EPA) + Isochrysis (DHA) — an algae enrichment, not an emulsion. 1–5 drops per portion of rotifers or nauplii, 6 h (their pages say 2–4 or 6–12), rinse before feeding.

library.name: Live rotifers (fridge bottle)
library.notes: Harvested from the cone through the 50 µm net; enrich a portion for DHA. The Cultures tab keeps this bottle's clock — add it here so the feed plans can pick it.

library.name: Live Tigriopus (from the tub)
library.notes: Nauplii through 50 µm, adults on 300 µm; pour into the refugium after lights-out.

eggTypes.name: Standard cysts (GSL)
eggTypes.note: The usual eBay/LFS cysts: 18–24 h at 26–30 °C, ~25 ppt, strong aeration.

eggTypes.name: Decapsulated cysts
eggTypes.note: Shell already dissolved — hatches faster (~16 h) and no shell separation.

eggTypes.name: High-hatch premium cysts
eggTypes.note: 90%+ hatch-rate grades tend to pop a little sooner (~20 h).

eggTypes.name: Cool room (below ~24 °C)
eggTypes.note: No heater on the hatcher? Budget up to 36 h — temperature rules the clock.

speciesLibrary.name: Sun coral (Tubastraea)
speciesLibrary.note: Target feeding is what works; broadcast alone leaves polyps unfed. Trainable to open in daylight by feeding at the same time daily.

speciesLibrary.name: Dendrophyllia / Balanophyllia
speciesLibrary.note: Sun-coral care but hungrier — more feeds, more volume.

speciesLibrary.name: Chili coral
speciesLibrary.note: Strictly nocturnal — feed after lights-out when the polyps are open; baby brine and decapsulated cysts are the perfect mouthful.

speciesLibrary.name: Gorgonians — Menella, Swiftia, Diodogorgia
speciesLibrary.note: The recommended starter NPS. Food must be no larger than the polyp mouth.

speciesLibrary.name: Gorgonians — Euplexaura, Guaiagorgia
speciesLibrary.note: Daily fine zooplankton, no days off.

speciesLibrary.name: Rhizotrochus typus
speciesLibrary.note: Whole meaty items by hand, 2–3× a week. Deepwater — runs happier cool.

speciesLibrary.name: Blueberry gorgonian (Acalycigorgia)
speciesLibrary.note: 'Cut flowers of the hobby.' Near-continuous micro-plankton, rotifers, oyster eggs. Expert-only, honestly.

speciesLibrary.name: Dendronephthya / Scleronephthya
speciesLibrary.note: Mostly a PHYTO feeder (weak nematocysts — 50–200× more carbon from phyto than zoo). The only proven method is a standing live-phyto density (5,000–50,000 cells/mL — a faint green tint), dosed continuously.

speciesLibrary.name: Sponges, tunicates, flame scallops
speciesLibrary.note: Obligate filter feeders; decline is invisible until it's late. Standing phyto density is what keeps them.

speciesLibrary.name: Feather star (crinoid)
speciesLibrary.note: Two documented long-term successes, ever. The working protocol: four feeds a day, each spread over two hours, indefinitely.

jars.name: Rotifers A

guard.line: the rack passes 30 °C in ~3 h (peak 36.7 °C, rack +3.9 °C over the room) — extra air, shade, feed lightly, a 50 % change ready

jars.tintTarget: leafy green — spinach, not pea soup
jars.note: Room temperature, no light, an open rigid airline to the cone tip at 1–2 bubbles/s (no airstone). Feed the concentrate to a leafy green, little and often: clear means hungry, still green at feed time means skip. Before a harvest: air off, settle, bleed the tip to waste, then 25 % a day through the 50 µm net — the water you take out IS the water change; refill with matched water. Sieve the whole cone into a clean one every fortnight, sooner on foam, milk or smell.

jars.name: Tigriopus B

guard.line: the rack passes 28 °C in ~1 h (peak 36.7 °C, rack +3.9 °C over the room) — extra air, shade, feed lightly, a 50 % change ready

jars.note: A flat tub, not a cone — they crawl. 35 ppt, 22–26 °C, open airline at 1–3 bubbles/s, loose lid, no light. Feed the Copepod Feed to a Granny Smith green, half rate in week one. A generation is a month: first harvest at four to six weeks, then no more than 25–30 % with 7–10 days between (50 µm keeps the nauplii, 300 µm the adults); put the harvested volume back as fresh water. Any ammonia = a 50 % change now. Warn at 28 °C: heat kills through oxygen and ammonia, not the animal — extra air, shade, feed lightly.

rig.caption: RESTART DUE — air off, settle, bleed the tip, the whole cone through the net into a clean one

profiles.name: Sunup
profiles.note: Gentle dawn ramp up from 0%. Warmer/low-blue start.

profiles.name: Midday
profiles.note: Peak — match your fixture to ~378–498 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ PAR at coral height.

profiles.name: Sunset
profiles.note: Gentle dusk ramp down to 0%. Sunset is the proximate spawn trigger — keep it smooth.

profiles.name: Moonlight
profiles.note: Dim blue (~1–2%). Real dark nights matter — light pollution desynchronises spawning.

temperature_heater.label: Heater (±0.2°C, tracks Season Table RT)
temperature_heater.code:
Fallback OFF
If Tmp < RT+-0.2 Then ON
If Tmp > RT+0.2 Then OFF
temperature_heater.note: RT is the seasonal reference temperature set by the Season Table.

temperature_chiller.label: Chiller (±0.2°C, tracks Season Table RT)
temperature_chiller.code:
Fallback OFF
If Tmp > RT+0.2 Then ON
If Tmp < RT+-0.2 Then OFF
temperature_chiller.note: Mirror of the heater — keeps the tank inside RT ± tolerance.

daylight_3step.label: Daylight — 3 step (sunrise / midday / sunset)
daylight_3step.target: Light virtual output or Profile selector
daylight_3step.code:
Fallback OFF
Set OFF
If Sun 000/-360 Then Sunup
If Sun 360/000 Then Sunset
If Sun 180/-180 Then Midday
daylight_3step.note: Sun NNN/NNN is minutes relative to the Season Table's sunrise/sunset.

daylight_5step.label: Daylight — 5 step (smoother ramps)
daylight_5step.target: Light virtual output or Profile selector
daylight_5step.code:
Fallback OFF
Set OFF
If Sun 000/-360 Then Sunup1
If Sun 090/-270 Then Sunup2
If Sun 180/-180 Then Midday
If Sun 270/-090 Then Afternoon
If Sun 360/000 Then Sunset
daylight_5step.note: Add Sunup1/Sunup2/Afternoon Profiles for a gentler dawn/dusk.

lunar_lsm.label: Lunar — moonrise→moonset (LSM / vMoon)
lunar_lsm.target: Lunar Simulation Module or vMoon virtual output
lunar_lsm.code:
Fallback OFF
Set OFF
If Moon 000/000 Then ON
lunar_lsm.note: Apex derives moon timing from the new-moon dates in the Season Table.

radion_moonlight.label: Radion moonlight (MXM) — follow vMoon
radion_moonlight.code: If Output vMoon = ON Then Moonlight
radion_moonlight.note: Switches the MXM-linked Radion to its Moonlight profile when vMoon is on.

walkthrough: Open Apex Local: in Apex Fusion click your Apex name (top-left) → Network → copy the IP, then open that IP in a browser and log in.
Go to the gear icon → wrench → sun icon to open the Season Table.
Enter the 12 monthly rows below: for each month set sunrise, sunset and the reference temperature (RT).
Enter the New-Moon dates below into the lunar / Season Table new-moon fields.
Create the four Profiles (Sunup, Midday, Sunset, Moonlight) for your MXM-linked Radions using the intensities below.
Paste the code snippets into the matching outlets/virtual outputs (heater, daylight, lunar, Radion moonlight).
⚠️ Re-check the Apex new-moon table every January 1 — it auto-resets, which silently drifts your lunar timing.

program.disclaimer: Curated reef presets with approximate monthly SST climatology. OpenReef generates the program; your Apex executes it with its own failsafes. Spawning needs sexually mature, same-species colonies, genuine dark nights, and many months of conditioning.
